back: An individual or group with an interest in a business that is affected by it or can affect it.
Internal: owners, managers, employees. External: customers, suppliers, lenders, government, the community and pressure groups.
Shareholders: profit and dividends. Workers: pay and security. Customers: quality and price. Lenders: repayment. Government: tax and law. Community: jobs and environment.
The obligation of managers and directors to explain and justify their decisions and results to those with a legitimate interest.
Conflict arises when aims differ, for example dividends against pay, or low prices against high profit. It can be reduced by communication, consultation and compromise.
Power over the business, interest in the decision, organisation, lack of alternatives for the firm and legal rights.
Shareholder view: the firm exists to earn a return for its owners. Stakeholder view: it must balance the interests of everyone affected.
Owners sell shares or vote out directors; workers strike or leave; customers switch; suppliers tighten terms; the community protests; pressure groups campaign.
